It is not acceptable at 2 blockers and 2 SHOULD-FIX: after D-104 it still makes historical schemas.v2 the normative adapter/corpus target while its current corpus rides accepted schemas.v11; its new archiveProfile does not define or emit a common archive serialization profile; and the report/exemption and corpus-generation mappings remain open. DR-120 and DR-103 remain OPEN; nothing is authorized.

blockers.title: The adapter and fixture contracts target historical schemas.v2 after D-104 accepted schemas.v11 as the current DR-103 successor
blockers.detail: At the pinned COORD bytes, D-104 records component-manifest-schemas.v11 (1c0b8868...) as DR-103's accepted schema successor and says D-013/schemas.v2 is historical. The pinned corpus-v3 catalog likewise declares schemas.v11 its ACCEPTED-SCHEMA-SUCCESSOR. V3 nevertheless says schemas.v2 is its emission/admission target and defines the fixture classes, while live ID-DEP-P2 still says the wider no-lock rule exists only in unaccepted schema successors. Accepted v11 itself carries the full-width no-lock rule and materially updated corpus conditionality. The contract therefore joins its production adapter to one schema lineage and its named current corpus to another.
blockers.impact: An emission or generated corpus can conform to the contract's historical target without conforming to the currently accepted DR-103 successor. OBL-1 and ID-DEP-8 are not a single reviewable canonical output contract at current authority.
blockers.minimumRepair: Issue a successor that pins and consumes schemas.v11 as the current emission/admission and testCorpusRequirements target, re-walks every mapped field/refusal/class against those bytes, and updates ID-DEP-P2's now-stale attribution. Keep schemas.v2 only as historical D-013 lineage. ArchiveDigest may remain on a precisely named later-schema ride because v11 does not carry that field.

blockers.title: archiveProfile claims archive determinism without defining or carrying a common archive profile
blockers.detail: The new profile says only that order and metadata use a 'named' rule and that compression, if any, is a 'named profile token'. It names no archive/container encoding, ordering algorithm, path/type/header encoding, metadata values, compression parameters, or closed token vocabulary. No emitted member or report field carries an archive-format/profile identifier; only archiveDigest is carried. Thus tar-like versus zip-like bytes, compressed versus uncompressed bytes, and multiple order/metadata choices all satisfy the prose while exposing different boundary formats. AT-3 exercises manifest TreeCommitment TC-PATH cases, but no class proves archive-entry-to-tree bijection, rejects an extra/unsafe archive entry, or exercises the profile's byte determinism.
blockers.impact: A common admission consumer cannot determine how to parse, reproduce, or safely compare the archive from the common contract. Per-language variation leaks past the adapter boundary, and CI-3's archive byte-identity claim has no closed profile to test.
blockers.minimumRepair: Define a tool-neutral, versioned archive serialization profile or a closed profile-token vocabulary carried in each per-platform emission/report; specify the one-to-one archive-to-TreeCommitment relation and deterministic ordering/metadata/compression rules; and pin that profile among CI inputs. This need not choose a packager, toolchain, or CLI.

shouldFix.title: The report still permits unpinned fixture claims and unrelated dependency rides as exemptions
shouldFix.detail: A produced TC-* or AT-* entry has no required {path, sha256} evidence join, and healthResultRef remains an unconstrained reference. A non-applicable or blocked entry need only cite any named ID-DEP-* or OD-*; the shape does not require that dependency to own that class, so an unrelated ride can self-exempt a required class. Exact joins for output members and gate results are a real repair, but the report is not yet exact-byte auditable across all claimed fixture results and its exemption set is not class-scoped.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Require {path, sha256} for every produced fixture/result and health result; define a closed class-to-lawful-ride mapping; reject missing, duplicate, or unrelated rides.

shouldFix.title: Separating hostile mutation from production emission dropped closed coverage of the DR-103 corpus
shouldFix.detail: FG-1 now normatively covers only TC-ACCEPT members, while AT-3 covers TC-PATH. fixtureGenerator says it produces examples of hostile classes followed by 'etc.', but no MUST enumerates every remaining nonconditional requirement. Current schema classes also include positive and behavioral cases outside TC-ACCEPT, such as lawful TC-DUP ownership-transfer/re-release cases, TC-NAME window behavior, TC-CLOSURE, and TC-METADATA-ONLY; they are not generated by an algorithm restricted to introducing exactly one invalidity.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Add a closed mapping from every applicable testCorpusRequirements member to production emission, test-only mutation, authored exact bytes, or behavioral harness generation, with expected outcome and {path, sha256} custody; keep hostile bytes impossible in S-3-EMIT.

Clarify whether runId is a deterministic input-derived key or a nondeterministic custody annotation excluded from the reproducible tuple; either interpretation is workable, but the current text leaves the two obligations in tension.

verdictBasis: 2 blockers, 2 SHOULD-FIX, 2 advisories. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: REJECT. The targeted v2 repairs are largely honest and several close cleanly, but the current candidate cannot be the DR-120 accepted design contract while it targets the historical DR-103 schema lineage, leaves archive serialization outside the common emitted contract, and retains report/exemption and corpus-generation gaps. This verdict does not mark DR-120 or DR-103 SATISFIED and authorizes no implementation.

authorityOfThisVerdict.note: Independent measurement only. Coordinator disposition is separate; both rows remain OPEN.
